legend: You are given a string s%%ZSMJ0%% of length n%%ZSMJ1%%, containing lowercase Latin letters.
Next you will be given a positive integer k%%ZSMJ2%% and two arrays, l%%ZSMJ3%% and r%%ZSMJ4%% of length k%%ZSMJ5%%.
It is guaranteed that the following conditions hold for these 2 arrays:
li≤ri%%ZSMJ8%%, for each positive integer i%%ZSMJ9%% such that 1≤i≤k%%ZSMJ10%%;
li=ri−1+1%%ZSMJ11%%, for each positive integer i%%ZSMJ12%% such that 2≤i≤k%%ZSMJ13%%;
Now you will be given a positive integer q%%ZSMJ14%% which represents the number of modifications you need to do on s%%ZSMJ15%%.
Each modification is defined with one positive integer x%%ZSMJ16%%:
Find an index i%%ZSMJ17%% such that li≤x≤ri%%ZSMJ18%% (notice that such i%%ZSMJ19%% is unique).
Let a=min%%ZSMJ20%% and let b=\max(x, r_i+l_i-x)%%ZSMJ21%%.
Reverse the substring of s%%ZSMJ22%% from index a%%ZSMJ23%% to index b%%ZSMJ24%%.

Reversing the substring [a, b]%%ZSMJ25%% of a string s%%ZSMJ26%% means to make s%%ZSMJ27%% equal to s_1, s_2, \dots, s_{a-1},\ s_b, s_{b-1}, \dots, s_{a+1}, s_a,\ s_{b+1}, s_{b+2}, \dots, s_{n-1}, s_n%%ZSMJ28%%.
Print s%%ZSMJ29%% after the last modification is finished.
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains a single integer t%%ZSMJ30%% (1 \le t \le 10^4%%ZSMJ31%%) — the number of test cases. Description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains two integers n%%ZSMJ32%% and k%%ZSMJ33%% (1 \le k \le n \le 2\cdot 10^5%%ZSMJ34%%) — the length of the string s%%ZSMJ35%%, and the length of arrays l%%ZSMJ36%% and r%%ZSMJ37%%.
The second line of each test case contains the string s%%ZSMJ38%% ( |s| = n%%ZSMJ39%%) containing lowercase Latin letters — the initial string.
The third line of each test case contains k%%ZSMJ40%% positive integers l_1, l_2, \dots, l_k%%ZSMJ41%% (1 \le l_i \le n%%ZSMJ42%%) — the array l%%ZSMJ43%%.
The fourth line of each test case contains k%%ZSMJ44%% positive integers r_1, r_2, \dots, r_k%%ZSMJ45%% (1 \le r_i \le n%%ZSMJ46%%) — the array r%%ZSMJ47%%.
The fifth line of each test case contains a positive integer q%%ZSMJ48%% (1 \le q \le 2 \cdot 10^5 %%ZSMJ49%%) — the number of modifications you need to do to s%%ZSMJ50%%.
The sixth line of each test case contains q%%ZSMJ51%% positive integers x_1, x_2, \dots, x_q%%ZSMJ52%% (1\le x_i \le n%%ZSMJ53%%) — the description of the modifications.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n%%ZSMJ54%% over all test cases does not exceed 2\cdot10^5%%ZSMJ55%%.
It is guaranteed that the sum of q%%ZSMJ56%% over all test cases does not exceed 2\cdot10^5%%ZSMJ57%%.
It is guaranteed that the conditions in the statement hold for the arrays l%%ZSMJ58%% and r%%ZSMJ59%%.
output: For each test case, in a new line, output the string s%%ZSMJ60%% after the last modification is done.
